items.title: Depot CI is now available in Origin
items.summary: Launching today in early beta, Origin code hosting features a Depot app to run your existing GitHub Actions workflows on Depot CI for better performance and reliability without GitHub.

items.title: Why I reimplemented LVM (with worse guarantees)
items.summary: Our microVMs launch in under a second, and assembling their block devices in parallel put LVM's roughly 100ms volume group-wide lock directly in the critical path. We kept the kernel's device-mapper, wrote our own control plane and gave up crash safety our ephemeral workloads never needed, making allocation roughly 100x faster.

items.title: How I delegate the work, not my judgment
items.summary: Agents can investigate, plan, and implement faster than I can, but reading a final diff is not the same as understanding why the system works the way it does. I own how the system behaves in production, so I want to keep building my intuition about it.

items.title: Why SOCI belongs in the build
items.summary: Most of a large container's startup goes to pulling and decompressing files it never reads to boot. SOCI makes the image seekable so the runtime loads only the bytes it needs, and Depot writes that index during the build, so the image can lazy-load the instant it's pushed.

items.title: Now available: Test results in your CI jobs
items.summary: Report JUnit from your Depot CI or Depot GitHub Actions jobs to see failures in context. A single command runs your suite and uploads the report. Split suites by historical timing and they'll automatically rebalance over time.

items.title: GitHub is the wrong shape for this new world
items.summary: GitHub isn't just falling short on performance and reliability. The whole collaboration paradigm is the wrong shape for how we build software now.

items.title: Improving system safety with Temporal Logic of Actions (TLA+)
items.summary: Formal verification never seemed worth it: writing a faithful TLA+ spec took too long. But now agents can write the spec from your code. We tried it on the rebuilt Depot Registry garbage collector, and the model checker found something our tests and reviews didn't: a race that could delete live data.

items.title: Depot is now available in Stripe Projects
items.summary: Depot is joining the Stripe Projects developer preview. Developers and their agents can now set up Depot from the terminal: create or link an organization, pick a plan, and get a token back that unlocks fast, reliable software delivery on Depot.

items.title: How we use PostHog to keep our AI assistant on track
items.summary: Keeping our AI assistant working well is a human responsibility at Depot. PostHog's AI engineering features turned our never-ending reviews into 30 minutes a week.

items.title: Why your team processes suck
items.summary: A team process without a principle underneath it is a real problem. Here's why the "why" is worth protecting as you scale.

items.title: Now available: Depot Code in private beta
items.summary: Source control has become the bottleneck at the top of the delivery loop. So we built our own: a diskless git server backed by blob storage that scales horizontally, mirrors your GitHub repos, and plugs straight into Depot CI. It's now in private beta.

items.title: Announcing Depot Metal
items.summary: Depot Metal is our next-generation compute and storage platform. Depot CI and Sandboxes are now running on it, with benchmarks showing workloads 30% faster and more optimizations on the way. You don't have to do anything to get it.

items.title: Failure fingerprints: Comparing test failures over time
items.summary: To make recurring test failures easier to reason about we needed to include historical context. Here's how we derive a stable identity for each test and a fingerprint for each failure, so you can tell a brand-new problem from the same flaky test you've seen a dozen times.

items.title: Staying in control of your codebase in the AI era
items.summary: AI can produce code faster than you can review it, but you're still the one on call when it breaks. You need an AI-assisted workflow you trust: linter guardrails, reference tests the agent can copy, tight AGENTS.md files, and PRs small enough to review. The goal isn't to avoid AI, it's to stay in control of what it ships.

items.title: Now available: Depot Sandbox SDK
items.summary: The same fast, isolated VMs that run Depot CI are now a programmable primitive you can drive from TypeScript. Boot a real microVM, run commands, and work with its filesystem, all from a few lines of code. The Sandbox SDK is in private beta.

items.title: Now available: SOCI v2 support for Depot container builds
items.summary: Depot container builds can now generate SOCI (Seekable OCI) v2 index metadata at build time, so a compatible runtime can lazy-load your images and start large containers in seconds instead of waiting on a full pull.

items.title: Now available: Step retry in Depot CI
items.summary: You can now tell Depot CI ahead of time that a step might need a retry. Add retry to a known-flaky step and Depot reruns just that step, not the expensive work before it.

items.title: Accelerating your test suite in CI
items.summary: Speeding up CI isn't one heroic refactor, it's a hunt for the next bottleneck, and for most teams the first one is the test suite. Here's how to attack it with parallelism, sharding, prebuilt images, and a job-density rule that keeps wider sharding from quietly torching your bill.

items.title: Observing Lambda durable functions
items.summary: Durable Lambda functions break most of the tracing assumptions you carry over from regular code. They replay from the top every time they wake, so spans get emitted twice, parent spans lose their children, and queue wait time hides in the gaps. Here's how we restored end-to-end visibility into Depot CI's durable functions.

items.title: Paranoia is baseline now: Security in the AI era
items.summary: Paranoid hardening has always been with us: aggressive kernel customizations for bug classes without a proven exploit, while Linux itself had a good-enough disclosure track record. Some of these hardenings became the default, some stayed controversial for a long time. AI-assisted vulnerability research made finding obscure vulnerabilities fast and cheap. So what does good enough even mean in this new era?

items.title: Now available: macOS 26 for GitHub Actions runners
items.summary: macOS 26 (Tahoe) is now available for Depot GitHub Actions runners. The `depot-macos-26` label runs on Apple M4 hardware with Xcode 26 and the macOS 26 SDKs preinstalled.

items.title: Now available: Depot CI API and CLI
items.summary: The Depot CI API and CLI are now generally available, so everything you could do in the dashboard you can now do from your terminal or hand off to an agent.

items.title: Depot CI run visibility in the dashboard
items.summary: The Depot CI dashboard shows you what ran, what failed, and where to look next. Follow recent workflow runs, browse activity by repository and workflow, and open any run to see exactly what happened.

items.title: Now available: Sherlock can analyze Depot CI workflows and jobs
items.summary: Sherlock can now analyze Depot CI workflows and jobs directly from the dashboard, using run context, attempts, step details, logs, summaries, and resource metrics to help you understand failures and slow jobs faster.

items.title: Speed up CI by running independent steps in parallel
items.summary: Most CI jobs run as one long serial script even when half the work doesn't depend on the other half. You can run independent steps in parallel for faster CI. We'll compare two ways to do it: shell backgrounding and Depot CI's parallel steps.

items.title: Now available: Nested virtualization support on Depot CI sandboxes
items.summary: We're excited to announce that Depot CI sandboxes now support nested virtualization which enables efficient Android Emulator usage.

items.title: Context isolation in coding agent loops
items.summary: The longer I worked on a problem with a coding agent, the dumber it felt. My context window was a junk drawer. Here's the multi-role loop I built so plans, builds, and reviews each get their own clean context.

items.title: How we got microVMs booting in under a second
items.summary: Depot CI's VM scheduler is just-in-time: no pre-warming, no warm pool of standby VMs. We stacked optimizations to get microVM cold boots from 7 to 9 seconds down to under a second, and this post walks through each one.

items.title: Building Depot CI with Lambda durable functions
items.summary: Depot CI's orchestrator runs on AWS Lambda durable functions. The orchestrator checkpoints state, suspends between events, and never burns compute while waiting. Here's how we designed the run-workflow-job hierarchy and the callback-driven orchestration loop that powers it.

items.title: How I run distributed Rust fuzzing in GitHub Actions
items.summary: With agents writing the initial fuzz harness, the hardest part of getting fuzzing into CI is basically gone. This is the setup I landed on: cargo fuzz, a GitHub Actions matrix job to fan work across multiple runners, and Actions cache to keep the corpus growing between runs.

items.title: Now available: OCI-compliant Depot Registry
items.summary: Depot Registry v2 is a ground-up rewrite of our container registry. The original design worked well as an ephemeral build store, but it had limitations around tags and repository naming. V2 solves those limitations and adds support for using it as a primary registry.

items.title: Migrating my workflows from GitHub Actions to Depot CI
items.summary: Depot CI runs GitHub Actions workflows on Depot infrastructure, and migrating is pretty seamless. Here's a walkthrough of moving an app's CI over, from installing the CLI to digging into logs.

items.title: What we need from CI for agentic engineering
items.summary: Agents can write and push code in seconds, but CI still takes minutes to give them feedback. That mismatch is the biggest bottleneck in agentic engineering today, and it's why CI needed to be rebuilt from scratch.

items.title: The end of push-wait-guess CI
items.summary: The old CI debugging loop goes: edit YAML, commit, push, wait, squint at logs, repeat. Depot CI replaces that with a local loop you can actually control, from running workflows against uncommitted changes to SSHing into the runner mid-job.

items.title: Now available: Depot CI
items.summary: We're excited to announce that Depot CI, our own programmable CI engine, is now generally available to everyone who wants to accelerate their CI in this new era of software engineering.

items.title: How I make support suck less
items.summary: Offload the scavenger-hunt grunt work to agents, log the useful bits (also with an agent) so the problem is discoverable next time, and spit out the day's support recap in seconds.

items.title: We've raised a $10M Series A from Felicis, Y Combinator, and Pioneer Fund
items.summary: We've raised a $10M Series A from Felicis, Y Combinator, and Pioneer Fund to build the next era of software delivery.

items.title: Now available: Sherlock can analyze your builds and CI
items.summary: Sherlock, our AI assistant, just got smarter. It can now analyze your builds and GitHub Actions jobs, break down your CI analytics, check your project settings, and even open support tickets on your behalf.

items.title: Lambda durable functions: Real implementation notes
items.summary: AWS Lambda durable functions let you write long-running processes that survive crashes and suspend compute entirely while waiting for external events. Getting them right requires understanding how replay works and the distinct failure modes of durable functions. Here's what we've learned from running durable functions for real.

items.title: How simulations reduce the guesswork in our infrastructure decisions
items.summary: We had a standby pool algorithm with over a dozen tunable parameters and no good way to test changes without risking real customer latency. So we built a simulator fed with real job data, ran hyperparameter optimization on it, and found a configuration that was faster and cheaper.

items.title: Now available: Depot skills
items.summary: The better the context you can give an agent, the better the results. Today we're publishing Depot skills: four structured skill files that give agents everything they need to use Depot correctly, installable with a single command.

items.title: The differences between QEMU microvm and Cloud Hypervisor
items.summary: microVMs are everywhere in 2026, especially for CI and sandboxes. But when you're building a platform, choosing between QEMU microvm and cloud-hypervisor isn't obvious. We compare API support, GPU passthrough, snapshotting, live migration, and hotplugging.

items.title: My intuition doesn't work anymore
items.summary: I used an LLM to refactor a 1500-line mess into clean, organized code. I realized months later that agents were the only ones working in it. They didn't need the clean code. They didn't need my empathy. My intuitions as an engineer just don't work anymore.

items.title: How we built Depot Wrapped 2025
items.summary: We built a fun Spotify Wrapped-style recap for Depot customers. Handling a year of data and making big numbers relatable was easy compared to teaching AI that "0.1 of a marathon" isn't exactly celebratory.

items.title: The bottleneck has shifted from writing code to integrating it
items.summary: AI can help write your feature in 20 minutes. But if your CI pipeline also takes 20 minutes, you've just traded one bottleneck for another. The bottleneck in software development has shifted from writing code to integrating it, and our workflows haven't caught up.

items.title: We instrumented GitHub Actions. Here's what GitHub won't show you.
items.summary: Optimizing GitHub Actions without telemetry is guesswork. We built CI telemetry into Depot to surface real metrics for every job, like CPU, memory, and logs. Here's how we wired it together with OpenTelemetry and scaled it with ClickHouse.

items.title: Optimize your Dockerfile for 5x faster builds
items.summary: Slow Docker builds are annoying and disrupt your flow. This guide shows practical techniques to optimize your Dockerfile, from simple instruction reordering to advanced caching strategies, with real measurements from a production-like Node.js application.

items.title: The 3 fears that make engineering suck
items.summary: I pegged every CPU in our ClickHouse cluster during my second week. The fix was quick, but it triggered the three fears that actually make engineering suck: looking dumb, underperforming, and wasting people's time.

items.title: What we learned optimizing EC2 macOS build performance
items.summary: We ran iOS builds across different EBS disk configurations on EC2 macOS instances to find the optimal setup. We discovered that simply throwing more IOPS at the problem doesn't work the way you'd expect.

items.title: What we learned accelerating 100 million builds in 2025
items.summary: 2025 was a big year for Depot. We helped accelerate over 100 million builds and helped incredible engineering teams save years of build time. Here's a look at the numbers and what we learned this year.
